claim: Copenhagen offbeat spots include the Barbie Museum (4,000+ Barbies, the only such collection in Denmark, by collector Lene Darlie Pedersen), the Geological Museum's 'One Room' of oddities (taxidermied polar bear, pickled specimens), and the Glyptotek's Nasothek of 100+ severed marble noses.
quote: the largest and only collection in Denmark with over 4,000 different Barbies... "One Room"... stuffed with all sorts of oddities including fossilised plants, a taxidermied polar bear and a host of pickled specimens

claim: Stockholm's unusual museums include the Spritmuseum (Museum of Spirits) and a Dala-horse museum tucked inside a souvenir shop.
quote: This small museum nestled inside a souvenir shop is dedicated to Sweden's most well-known toy.

claim: Vrak – Museum of Wrecks (Djurgården, Stockholm) is an interactive maritime museum focused on sunken ships and Baltic underwater archaeology.
quote: This maritime museum focuses on sunken ships, archaeological treasures, and the mysteries that lie beneath the waves.

claim: Stockholm's Toy Museum displays about 40,000 toys in a 2,500 sqm former torpedo workshop underground on Skeppsholmen.
quote: The Stockholm Toy Museum boasts about 40,000 toys on display, showcased in a unique underground location, a 2,500 square-meter former torpedo workshop on the museum island of Skeppsholmen.

claim: Oslo's Mini Bottle Gallery is billed as the only museum of its kind in the world, with ~50,000 miniature bottles across three storeys (some containing fruit, worms or mice) plus a 'horror room'.
quote: Houses the world's largest collection of miniature bottles with 53,000 specimens displayed across a 3-story building. Bottles contain unusual contents ranging from fruits and berries to worms and mice.

claim: Oslo's Norsk Tryllemuseum (Norway Museum of Magic) shows posters, props and gear and opens only Sundays 1pm-4pm with a 2pm magic show.
quote: The Norsk Tryllemuseum (Norway Museum of Magic) is a collection of posters, props, photographs and gear, and the museum is only open on Sundays from 1pm-4pm with a magic show at 2pm.

claim: Helsinki's Hotel and Restaurant Museum at the Cable Factory runs a multisensory 'Taste Matters' exhibition on Finnish culinary culture; one ticket also covers the Theatre Museum and Finnish Museum of Photography in the same complex.
quote: The permanent exhibition "Taste Matters" is an adventure appealing to all senses. You can experience the Hotel and Restaurant Museum, the Theatre Museum and the Finnish Museum of Photography with one ticket.

claim: Reykjavik's Icelandic Phallological Museum displays over 300 penises from 100+ species (website lists 280 from 93), draws ~70,000 visitors/year, opens daily, and in December 2024 added the largest verified human penis cast (Matt Barr, 36cm).
quote: the museum began displaying a confirmed erect plaster cast of Matt Barr, measuring over 36cm, the largest ever verified cast of a human penis.

claim: Icelandic Phallological Museum admission is 2750 ISK (~USD 20) with 20% off via Reykjavik City Card and free entry for children 13 and under; it has relocated to a larger harbour-side space with a phallic-themed bistro.
quote: Admission costs 2750 ISK (roughly 20 USD), with a 20% discount available with Reykjavik City Card, and children aged 13 and under enter free.

claim: Tallinn's Hotel Viru KGB Museum occupies a secret 23rd-floor radio centre from which KGB agents spied on foreign guests during the Soviet era; visited by guided tour.
quote: KGB agents occupied a radio center on the secret 23rd floor from which they would spy on foreign guests.

claim: Tallinn's Kalev Marzipan Museum at Café Maiasmokk (Estonia's oldest café) lets visitors watch marzipan figures hand-painted, while the separate Marzipan Gallery shows elaborate marzipan sculptures of city sights.
quote: there's a small marzipan museum in the café where you can watch intricate marzipan fancies being decorated while you sip your cappuccino

claim: Tallinn's KGB Prison Cells museum (Pagari 1) preserves the Soviet basement prison with six cells and a solitary confinement cell; admission about €10, open daily 10-18.
quote: located at Pagari 1... with hours Mon-Sun 10-18 and admission €10. The basement was turned into a prison... two narrow corridors containing six cells and one solitary confinement cell.
